passages.note: Floor vote on HB2822, a general personal-property depreciation schedule bill, not a business-attraction incentive deal.

passages.provision_quote: For personal property that is initially classified during or after tax year 2022 as class one, paragraph 8, 9, 10 or 13 pursuant to section 42-12001 personal property that is initially classified during or after tax year 2022 as class two (P) pursuant to section 42-12002 and personal property that is acquired during or after tax year 2022 and initially classified during or after tax year 2022 as class six pursuant to section 42-12006, paragraph 2 or 3, the assessor shall use a valuation factor of two and one-half percent.
passages.note: The enacted provision is a uniform statewide depreciation valuation factor for all qualifying personal property, not a targeted business-attraction incentive.
Bill overview names Weninger as Prime sponsor of HB2822, a general depreciation-schedule bill signed into law.

rows.reasoning: HB2822, which Weninger prime-sponsored and voted for, amends the statewide depreciation schedule for locally assessed personal property; it applies uniformly to all qualifying taxpayers with no reference to attracting a business, no wage or hiring conditions, no clawback, and no distinction between large and small employers. That is a different question from the ladder's, which orders incentive deals used to attract businesses by size and by whether conditions or limits attach, so this evidence is adjacent rather than on-question.
